one_liner: 47-line Zig blocking TCP responder whose 2x wrk lead over C/C++ comes from skipping the request read, not codegen.
what_it_does: blade_core.zig is a toy single-threaded server, not a library: it opens a socket with SO_REUSEADDR, binds 0.0.0.0:8083, listens with backlog 128, then loops accept, write a fixed 40-byte 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK / Content-Length: 2 / OK' response, close. It uses std.posix calls and a hand-declared sockaddr_in struct with a local htons; there is no parsing, routing, keep-alive or concurrency. The C and C++ siblings in the same repo do the same thing but call read() once before writing.
how_it_is_fast: It is not faster at the same work. The Zig loop writes the response the moment accept returns and never waits for the client's request, so each connection costs accept, write and close; the C/C++ loops add a blocking read() that waits for wrk's request before they can write and accept the next connection. In a single-threaded blocking server that saved wait per connection, not Zig code generation (the Zig binary is an unoptimised Debug build), explains the 80,700 vs 40,715/32,976 req/s gap. Closing a socket with the request still unread makes the kernel reset the connection, which fits the 701k wrk write errors, about 0.87 per completed response (derived from page data: 80,700 req/s x 10 s = 807k).
when_to_use: As a 47-line example of raw std.posix socket calls (socket, setsockopt, bind, listen, accept, write) in Zig 0.12, before std.posix was reshuffled in later releases.
As a cautionary benchmark case: a responder that answers before reading the request inflates wrk req/s and produces reset connections.
Not for any production or comparative use; the repo publishes no harness that measures equal work.
when_not_to_use: As evidence that Zig beats C or C++ on networking: the Zig server does less work (no read), is built in Debug against gcc/g++ -O2, and the run reports 701k write errors against 0 for C and C++.
As an HTTP server of any kind: it ignores the request entirely, sends no Connection: close header although it closes after every reply, and serves one connection at a time.
Under load you care about: every write or accept error is propagated with try out of main, so one failed syscall ends the process.
On later Zig releases: the code targets Zig 0.12 std.posix and std.io.getStdOut APIs (the banner and README say 0.12.0+); it is not tested on anything newer.

integration.dependencies: none (Zig standard library only); benchmarking needs wrk
integration.min_toolchain: Zig 0.12.0 (source banner; the repo commits zig-linux-x86_64-0.12.0.tar.xz and a binary linked by LLD 17.0.6)
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 as published (POSIX sockets; other targets not documented)
integration.thread_safety: single-threaded blocking accept loop; no shared state

gotchas: Harness flaw: blade_core.zig never reads the request, while blade_core.c and blade_core.cpp read() once before writing; under a single-threaded blocking loop this removes a wait per connection and makes the close abortive, so the req/s column compares different work.

Build mismatch: the Makefile's blade_zig target runs a bare 'zig build-exe blade_core.zig' (Debug mode), which writes a binary named blade_core, not blade_zig as README and bench instructions say; the committed blade_core binary is a 2.25 MB statically linked ELF with debug info and runtime-safety symbols, i.e. the Debug build, against gcc -O2 and g++ -O2 (Rust is plain rustc, also unoptimised).

No raw wrk output is in the repo although the README points to performance_summary.md for 'detailed logs'; it holds only the summary table, so the 0-error C/C++ rows and the 701k Zig write errors cannot be checked. No CPU, kernel, compiler or wrk versions, single run, servers on different ports, and only the Zig server sets SO_REUSEADDR.

Every connection is closed after one reply while wrk -c1000 expects keep-alive, so all four rows mostly measure TCP connect and teardown on loopback with a 128-entry listen backlog against 1000 connections.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Never as a server: zix (Zig HTTP server) and libxev (Zig event loop) have HttpArena rows against nginx, h2o and Drogon on a shared harness; the bladebench Rust row shares this repo's harness and its Debug/-O2 mismatch but at least reads the request, so neither bladebench row is a language comparison.
verified_claims_summary: One first-party wrk run (-t8 -c1000 -d10s, loopback, hardware and versions not stated) gave the Zig Debug build 80,700 req/s against 40,715 for g++ -O2 C++ and 32,976 for gcc -O2 C (1.98x and 2.45x, derived from page data), with 701k write errors on the Zig row only; the Zig server skips the request read, so the lead reflects less work and reset connections rather than faster code.
status_note: Single 'Initial Commit' on 2025-07-12, 0 stars, 0 issues, MIT; stale toy benchmark that also commits a built binary and the Zig 0.12.0 toolchain tarball, useful only as a small socket example.
